card.name: Second digit inside dose numbers
card.fires_on: A single digit in the middle of a multi-digit number, usually right after the first digit, in dose instructions. It is typically followed by mg, mcg or a decimal such as .5.

modes.label: Digit in a dose amount
modes.description: The second digit of a number giving a dose, split into separate digits before mg or mcg.
modes.example: Reduce dose by 1<<1>> mg once daily.

modes.label: Digit before a decimal
modes.description: A digit before a decimal point in a starting dose for a drug.
modes.example: start bosentan at 6<<2>>.5 mg once daily or every other

modes.label: Digit in a day count
modes.description: A digit inside a number of days or a maximum dose per kg.
modes.example: after a total of 4<<5>> days, therapy should be discontinued.

card.plain: It fires on the middle digit of a dose number, like the 1 in 11 mg, when the number is written out digit by digit.
